content: 1. The 2014 guidelines for managing patients with valvular heart disease were developed by the American College of Cardiology (ACC) and the American Heart Association (AHA) Task Force on Practice Guidelines. These guidelines were published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology (Volume 63, Issue 22, Pages 57-185). The publication is identified by ISSN 1558-3597. 2. In 2008, the ACC and AHA released an updated guideline focusing on valvular heart disease, specifically addressing the management of infective endocarditis. This update was endorsed by the Society of Cardiovascular Anesthesiologists, the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions, and the Society of Thoracic Surgeons. The report was published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology (Volume 52, Issue 8, Pages 676-685) and is associated with ISSN 1558-3597 and PMID 18702976. 3. The European Society of Cardiology (ESC) published updated guidelines in 2009 for the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of infective endocarditis. This task force report was endorsed by the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (ESCMID) and the International Society of Chemotherapy (ISC) for Infection and Cancer. The guidelines appeared in the European Heart Journal (Volume 30, Issue 19, Pages 2369-2413) and are identified by DOI 10.1093/eurheartj/ehp285, ISSN 1522-9645, and PMID 19713420. 4. The American Heart Association (AHA) released guidelines in 2007 for the prevention of infective endocarditis. These guidelines were developed by the AHA Rheumatic Fever, Endocarditis, and Kawasaki Disease Committee, in collaboration with the AHA Council on Cardiovascular Disease in the Young, the AHA Council on Clinical Cardiology, the AHA Council on Cardiovascular Surgery and Anesthesia, and the Quality of Care and Outcomes Research Interdisciplinary Working Group. The report was published in Circulation (Volume 116, Issue 15, Pages 1736-1754) and is associated with DOI 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.106.183095, ISSN 1524-4539.
